13.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -a marks the accusative case, signaling it is the direct object (the thing acted upon); the ending -kum means 'your' for a group being addressed.

1.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
1.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

2.meaning: He asks you for it — the verb 'to ask/request' carrying both the person asked and the thing asked for inside the single word.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb, third person masculine singular, Form I: the ya- prefix means 'he'. The stem itself takes no final vowel, marking the jussive mood — the clipped form used in conditional clauses and after 'do not'. Two object pronouns are stacked on the end; when '-kum' is followed by another pronoun it lengthens to '-kumū' for ease of pronunciation. The final -hā refers back to something grammatically feminine.

3.meaning: And then he presses you hard — to importune, to push a request to its limit and insist until every last thing is squeezed out; the causative sense of exhausting someone with demands.

parts.en: he (third person masculine subject prefix of a causative verb)

3.grammar: 'fa-' is the connector 'so/then', linking an action as the immediate result of what came before. The verb is present tense, third person masculine singular, Form IV (causative); the yu- prefix with its u-vowel is the signature of this pattern and means 'he'. The stem is a weak-ended verb whose long final vowel has been dropped (yuḥfī → yuḥfi), which marks the jussive mood — the shortened form used in conditions and after 'do not'. The attached -kum is the object 'you (all)'.

4.meaning: You are stingy, you hold back — to grip what one has and refuse to give it out, withholding wealth or good from others out of miserliness.
4.grammar: Present-tense verb, second person masculine plural, Form I: the ta- prefix (with an a-vowel, as Form I takes) means 'you', and the -ū ending marks a masculine plural subject. The absence of the usual -na (-ū, not -ūna) shows the subjunctive/jussive mood, the form a verb takes after particles of purpose or negation, or in the answer-clause of a condition.

5.meaning: And he brings out, produces, or exposes — the causative sense of 'to go out': to make something emerge from where it was concealed or contained.

parts.en: he (third person masculine subject prefix of a causative verb)

5.grammar: 'wa' is the connector 'and'. The verb is present tense, third person masculine singular, Form IV (causative — 'to make something come out'); the yu- prefix with its u-vowel signals this pattern and means 'he'. The final consonant carries no vowel, which marks the jussive mood — the clipped form used in conditional sentences, in commands, and after 'do not'.

6.meaning: Your deep-seated grudges — the buried rancour and ill-will that a person harbours inwardly toward others, hidden malice rather than open anger.
6.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with a possessive pronoun attached. The -a ending is accusative, the case a noun takes when it is the object of a verb or governed by certain particles. The attached -kum means 'your (of you all)', and because the noun is possessed it is already definite without needing 'the'.

1.meaning: An attention-drawing phrase meaning 'here you are! / lo, you are these' — a particle of alerting ('here, behold') fused to the pronoun 'you (plural)', used to call attention to the addressees and their situation.
1.grammar: Built from the alerting particle hā ('here!, behold!') prefixed to the standalone pronoun antum ('you', masculine plural). The pronoun antum is the form used for the subject/topic — 'you all'. Together they draw attention: 'Here you are, you are the ones who…'.

2.meaning: 'These' — a demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things that are near ('these ones, these here').
2.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'these,' used for near things or people (of either gender). It is built on a fixed base, but its final vowel reflects case: the -i here is the genitive form (hāʾulāʾi), required because it falls in a genitive position governed by the preceding preposition. This contrasts with the nominative form hāʾulāʾu — so the -i is a genuine case marker, not merely a connecting vowel.

3.meaning: To be summoned, invited, or called upon. This is the passive of the verb 'to call/invite' (daʿā): the subject is the one being called, with no statement of who does the calling, addressed to a group: 'you all are being called'.

parts.en: you (masculine plural subject; passive imperfect prefix)
be called / be invited (passive stem of daʿā)

3.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) passive verb. The tu-…-na frame marks a masculine-plural 'you' subject, and the internal vowelling (u-then-a) makes it passive, so the subject receives the action: 'you are being called' rather than 'you call'. The imperfect form signals action that is ongoing, repeated, or general rather than completed.
3.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invite, pray

4.meaning: So that you may spend — to lay out wealth and disburse it, to expend what one has rather than hoard it; the causative sense of 'to make something go out and be used up'.

parts.en: you (masculine plural subject prefix of a causative verb)

4.grammar: 'li-' is the particle of purpose, 'so that / in order that', and it forces the verb after it into the subjunctive. The verb is present tense, second person masculine plural, Form IV (causative); the tu- prefix with its u-vowel is the mark of Form IV and means 'you', and the -ū ending marks a masculine plural subject. The dropped -na (-ū, not -ūna) is precisely the mark of that subjunctive mood.

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
6.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: So among you / then some of you — a compound expressing that a portion of the addressed group belongs to one category, literally 'then from you (all)'.
8.grammar: Built entirely of particles and a pronoun: fa- links what follows to what came before ('so, then'); min is the preposition 'from/among'; -kum is the attached pronoun 'you all' (masculine/mixed plural). The pairing min + kum typically introduces a subgroup: 'some of you are…'.
8.root: — (particles + pronoun; no root)

9.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
9.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

10.meaning: He is stingy, he withholds — to cling to what one possesses and refuse to part with it.
10.grammar: Present-tense verb, third person masculine singular, Form I: the ya- prefix means 'he'. The final -u ending is the indicative, the default mood of a verb that stands as a plain statement of fact — nothing before it is bending it into a purpose clause, a condition, or a prohibition.

11.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
11.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

12.meaning: He is stingy, he withholds — to clutch what one has and refuse to give it out.
12.grammar: Present-tense verb, third person masculine singular, Form I: the ya- prefix means 'he'. The final consonant carries no vowel at all (bkhal, not bkhalu) — this bare ending marks the jussive mood, the form used after 'if', after 'do not', and in commands; it typically signals that the verb hangs on a condition rather than asserting a fact.

13.meaning: A compound particle 'so it is only …' or 'then indeed only.' It joins a consequence ('so/then') to an emphatic restriction ('only / nothing more than'), confining the statement to exactly what follows.
13.grammar: A cluster of particles: 'fa-' introduces a result ('so/then'), 'inna' gives emphasis ('truly'), and the attached 'mā' turns the emphasis into restriction, so the whole means 'so it is only/nothing but.' These are connective and emphatic words; they have no case ending of their own.

14.meaning: He is stingy, he withholds — to cling to what one possesses and refuse to part with it.
14.grammar: Present-tense verb, third person masculine singular, Form I: the ya- prefix means 'he'. The final -u ending is the indicative, the default mood of a verb that stands as a plain statement of fact — nothing before it is bending it into a purpose clause, a condition, or a prohibition.

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

15.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

16.meaning: His own self, soul, or person — 'nafs' (self/soul/life) bound to 'his.'
16.grammar: A feminine noun 'nafs' with the attached possessive '-hi' ('his'). The '-i' ending is genitive, here because the word follows a preposition or is the possessed term in 'the self OF him'; the pronoun takes the form '-hi' after that 'i' sound.
16.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath, living being

17.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
17.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
17.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

18.meaning: The Self-Sufficient / the Free-of-Need / the Rich — the One utterly independent and in need of nothing, possessing all wealth; as a human trait it means rich or free from want.
18.grammar: An intensive adjective on the 'faʿīl' pattern (denoting a deep, established quality), with 'the'. The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as a subject or the thing being described.
18.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be free of need, rich, self-sufficient

19.meaning: 'And you' — the standalone pronoun for a group being addressed, used to emphasise or single out the persons spoken to.

parts.en: connecting vowel before a following word

19.grammar: A prefix wa- ('and') joined to the detached subject pronoun antum, second person masculine plural ('you all'). The added final -u (giving antumu) is a helping vowel inserted to ease pronunciation when the next word begins with a definite article; it carries no case meaning of its own.

20.meaning: The poor, the needy — those in a state of want and dependence, lacking the means to meet their own needs and therefore reliant on others.
20.grammar: A definite broken (irregular) plural noun: 'al-' is the definite article 'the'. The final -u ending is nominative, the case a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the thing being described in a statement of identity ('X IS …').

21.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
21.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

22.meaning: 'You turn away' / 'you turn your backs' — to turn aside, retreat, or shun, often implying rejecting or abandoning something. Addressed to a group.
22.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form V, 'to turn oneself away') addressed to a group of males ('you all'). The 'ta-' prefix marks the second person, and the final '-aw/-ū' element marks the plural subject. The shortened form (without a final 'n') signals the subjunctive/jussive — used after particles like 'if' or 'lest,' giving a sense such as 'if you turn away.'
22.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near; to turn toward or away, take charge

23.meaning: He substitutes, exchanges one thing for another — to put a replacement in the place of what was there before, seeking or bringing about a swap.

parts.en: Form X marker (seeking / bringing about the action)

23.grammar: Present-tense verb, third person masculine singular, Form X — the pattern with the 'sta-' element, which typically conveys seeking or bringing about the action of the root, here 'to get a replacement'. The ya- prefix means 'he'. The final consonant takes no vowel, marking the jussive mood: the clipped form used in conditions, commands, and after 'do not'.

24.meaning: 'A people, a folk, a community' — a group of human beings bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared standing.
24.grammar: An indefinite collective noun. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) marks it as the object of an action.
24.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group, people

25.meaning: "other than you / a people other than you" — ghayr expresses 'other-than, different from, not'; with 'you all' attached it means 'others besides you'.
25.grammar: The noun ghayr ('other-than'), used to negate or exclude, with an attached pronoun. The -a ending is the accusative case, used for a direct object or a similar complement. The suffix -kum means 'you all', so the whole means 'other-than-you / others besides you'.

26.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
26.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

27.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
27.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

28.meaning: They are, they become, they come to be — the verb of simply being or turning out to be a certain way, which links a subject to a description rather than naming an action.

parts.en: they / he (third person masculine subject prefix)

28.grammar: Present-tense verb, third person masculine plural, Form I: the ya- prefix marks third person and the -ū ending marks a masculine plural subject, 'they'. The missing -na (-ū, not -ūna) shows the subjunctive/jussive mood, the form used after particles of purpose or negation and in conditional clauses. As a verb of 'being', it normally puts the following description into the accusative case.
28.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

29.meaning: Your likes, those similar to you — counterparts or matches resembling you, bound to a 'your'. The plural of 'a like / equivalent'.
29.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun meaning 'likenesses/counterparts', with the accusative ending -a (the case that commonly marks a direct object) and the attached pronoun -kum, 'your / of you' (masculine plural).
